beforeImage.name: Revolution Wind & South Fork Wind
beforeImage.description: Revolution Wind and South Fork Wind are offshore wind projects serving the Northeast U.S. power market. Their end markets are utility-scale electricity systems in Rhode Island, Connecticut, and New York that require contracted renewable generation and related transmission infrastructure. The projects follow an asset-heavy model characteristic of offshore wind, with economics tied to long-term offtake arrangements, construction execution, and operation of large-scale generation assets. South Fork Wind reached commercial operations first, while Revolution Wind has been under construction for the regional offshore market. In 2024, Eversource completed the sale of its 50% stakes in both projects to Global Infrastructure Partners’ Skyborn Renewables, leaving Ørsted and Skyborn as joint venture partners. Public disclosures reviewed do not provide a combined employee count or revenue figure for the two-project ownership structure.

afterImage.name: Revolution Wind & South Fork Wind
afterImage.description: Revolution Wind & South Fork Wind is a paired manager-level record for two separate contracted U.S. offshore-wind project companies: Revolution Wind, LLC and South Fork Wind, LLC. South Fork is a 132 MW, 12-turbine project serving Long Island that entered commercial operation on March 14, 2024. Revolution is a 704 MW, 65-turbine project serving Rhode Island and Connecticut; it first delivered power on March 13, 2026 and was more than 95% complete in August 2026. GIP IV Whale/designated affiliates acquired Eversource's 50% interests in both projects on September 30, 2024, with Skyborn Renewables managing those interests. Ørsted retains the other 50% of each project, and Eversource is retained as the former 50% partner. BlackRock's acquisition of GIP closed after the project transaction and did not create a separate BlackRock ownership period. No later sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.
